_comment: The file-layout contract (GH #292), in machine-readable form.
One row per file the Overnight Agent reads or writes. Each row answers four
questions: who OWNS the intent, who is allowed to WRITE it, whether it is on the
PER-RUN READ PATH, and what BOUNDS its size.
The invariant this file exists to enforce:
That combination is the bug. It produced GH #262 on user-settings.md (grew to
~947,000 chars, ~97% of the context window per call, runs stopped finishing) and
GH #291 on the journals (task-400.md at 257 KB / ~66K tokens, read whole when
planning that task). Declaring it as data means the third instance is refused
before it is written rather than diagnosed after it breaks something.
read-path-budget-sweep.mjs enforces this. It only ever reads.

files.retention: values only; the agent's prose belongs in agent-lore.md
files.note: Writer is 'app' as the target state (GH #292). The agent appending here is what caused #262; SKILL.md now redirects those writes to agent-lore.md.

files.retention: reviewed edits only; guardrail prose splits per GH #127
files.note: Developer-written, so it cannot grow unattended. Budgeted anyway because it is read in full on every run.

files.retention: a visible list the user edits; bounded by fitting on one screen
files.note: Shipped by #290, and READ by the agent since #297 (`oa-state.ps1 gate`, PHASE 0). The agent only ever READS this file, which is what makes anything in it attributable to the user without a marker (#250) -- writer stays 'app' for that reason and must never become 'agent'. Budgeted tightly on purpose: its value is that the whole gate is reviewable at a glance, and a gate nobody reads is a gate nobody trusts.
Agent-written, so it MUST stay off the per-run read path. Unbudgeted on purpose: it is grepped, never loaded. If this ever becomes 'every-run' the contract check fails, which is the point.

files.retention: none today - this is the open defect

contractException.reason: SKILL.md instructs the agent to read a task's linked journal(s) in full before planning. Closing this needs a bounded extract (head + latest turn + open asks), not a size cap, so the violation is acknowledged and tracked rather than silenced. Growth beyond tolerance still fails.

files.note: SKILL.md says to read a task's linked journal(s) in full before planning. 95th percentile is ~41 KB, so 64 KB is above normal and flags genuine outliers rather than routine files.
files.idPatternNote: A real journal is task-<id>.md. The glob also matches OneDrive sync-conflict copies (task-463-DESKTOP-P9116M3.md), which no run reads -- oa-state.ps1 scan returned exactly 239 rows on 2026-09-01, the same count as files matching this pattern. Declaring the read-path SHAPE is deliberate: matching the conflict shape instead would need a guess per sync vendor and would miss a custom machine name.
files.strayPatternNote: SEPARATE FROM idPattern ON PURPOSE, and the separation is load-bearing. idPattern decides what is MEASURED; strayPattern decides what is ACCUSED. The folder also holds 153 legitimate deliverables that SKILL.md tells the agent to write as task-<id>-<slug>.md, and a conflict copy has the same shape as one. Collapsing the two would print 'remedy is to remove it' against the user's own deliverables. Files matching neither pattern are counted as companions and nothing is claimed about them. Keep this pattern NARROW: too narrow leaves a conflict copy uncounted, too wide accuses a deliverable, and those costs are not symmetric. Extend it only for a naming form actually observed on disk.
